nodes.title: Relational database basics
nodes.why: Will enable writing correct queries against the historian and outage databases.
checkpoints: A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table.
A foreign key creates a relationship between tables.
Normalization reduces data redundancy by splitting data into related tables.
Queries that reference non‑existent columns cause an error because the column cannot be resolved.

nodes.title: Python basics
nodes.why: Will provide the scripting foundation for data processing tasks.
checkpoints: Python uses indentation to define code blocks, so inconsistent indentation raises a SyntaxError.
Variables are dynamically typed, meaning the type can change at runtime.
The import statement loads modules, allowing access to additional functions.
The standard print function writes text to standard output, which is visible in the console.

nodes.title: Time‑series fundamentals
nodes.why: Will support handling of hourly and five‑minute load records.
checkpoints: A timestamp with uniform intervals defines a regular time series.
Missing timestamps create gaps that must be imputed for analysis.
Daylight saving shifts cause duplicate or missing hours, requiring adjustment.
Aggregating data to a coarser granularity sums or averages values over each interval.

nodes.title: SQL queries
nodes.why: Will extract load, generation, and outage records from the historian databases to support analysis.
checkpoints: SELECT statements retrieve columns from tables, so the column list determines output.
WHERE filters rows before aggregation, so rows not meeting the condition are excluded.
ORDER BY sorts the result set, affecting the presentation but not the underlying data.
Using aliases simplifies column references, especially when joining tables with identical column names.

nodes.title: SQL joins
nodes.why: Will combine hourly and five‑minute tables to create a unified view for reporting.
checkpoints: An INNER JOIN returns only rows with matching keys in both tables, discarding non‑matches.
A LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the left table and fills missing right columns with NULL.
Joining on mismatched data types causes an error because the comparison cannot be performed.
Join conditions must reference columns from each table, otherwise the result creates a Cartesian product.

nodes.title: Pandas data manipulation
nodes.why: Will manipulate extracted data in Python to clean and prepare it for dashboards.
checkpoints: DataFrames store columnar data with labeled axes, enabling column selection by name.
The .loc accessor selects rows by label, so it includes the endpoint in slices.
.apply applies a function across rows or columns, allowing custom transformations.
Merging DataFrames on keys aligns rows, and mismatched keys result in NaN values.

nodes.title: Time‑series data cleaning
nodes.why: Will resolve gaps, meter errors, and daylight‑saving shifts to ensure accurate time‑series analysis.
checkpoints: Detecting gaps involves checking for missing timestamps in the expected sequence.
Outliers from meter errors are often replaced or removed because they distort analysis.
Daylight saving adjustments shift timestamps forward or backward, creating duplicate hours.
Interpolation fills missing values based on neighboring points, preserving continuity.

nodes.title: Power BI dashboard development
nodes.why: Will create interactive visualizations for operators and planners to monitor grid performance.
checkpoints: Power BI reports use visual tiles that refresh when the underlying dataset updates.
Data model relationships define how tables link, so incorrect relationships cause wrong totals.
DAX measures compute aggregations, and incorrect formulas produce misleading values.
Publishing a dashboard shares it with workspace users, granting them view permissions.

nodes.title: Load forecast evaluation
nodes.why: Will assess forecast accuracy by comparing predicted and actual loads and identify major discrepancies.
checkpoints: Mean absolute error calculates the average absolute difference between forecast and actual loads.
Forecast bias is identified when errors consistently have the same sign.
Seasonal patterns repeat at regular intervals, so errors may be larger during peak seasons.
Comparing forecasts to actuals requires aligning timestamps, otherwise mismatched periods distort error metrics.

nodes.title: Grid supply‑demand basics
nodes.why: Will understand how electricity supply matches demand to contextualize analysis of grid metrics.
checkpoints: Supply must equal demand at each instant, so any imbalance triggers frequency deviation.
Generators adjust output to follow load changes, because the grid frequency signals excess or shortage.
Transmission constraints limit power flow, causing congestion that requires dispatch adjustments.
Balancing authorities schedule resources ahead of time to maintain reliability.

nodes.title: Documentation and reproducibility
nodes.why: Will record metric definitions so colleagues can repeat calculations without ambiguity.
checkpoints: Including data source references lets others locate the original tables.
Describing each transformation step enables reconstruction of the metric.
Versioning scripts ensures that changes can be traced and rolled back if needed.
Clear metric definitions prevent divergent interpretations among analysts.

nodes.title: Clear technical writing
nodes.why: Will communicate findings in language accessible to non‑analyst stakeholders.
checkpoints: Writing in plain language avoids jargon that can confuse non‑technical readers.
Structured headings guide readers through sections, improving navigation.
Using bullet points lists steps concisely, so each action is isolated.
Defining acronyms on first use eliminates ambiguity for unfamiliar audiences.

nodes.title: SCADA data overview
nodes.why: Will handle SCADA time‑series if available to enrich operational insights.
checkpoints: SCADA systems collect real‑time measurements from field devices, providing current operational data.
Tag naming conventions standardize identifiers, so inconsistent names cause lookup errors.
Historian archives SCADA data, enabling retrieval of past measurements for analysis.
Data latency occurs when transmission delays postpone real‑time values, affecting timeliness.

nodes.title: Weather data integration
nodes.why: Will incorporate weather variables to explain load variations when needed.
checkpoints: Weather APIs deliver forecasts in JSON, requiring parsing to extract relevant fields.
Temperature and wind speed correlate with load, so they are often used as explanatory variables.
Missing weather observations are imputed using nearby stations, because gaps hinder model training.
Time alignment matches weather timestamps to load data, ensuring accurate feature engineering.
